symptoms.summary: Memory read traffic (GM or L2) dominates the measured path while compute waits on it.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Profile attributes a large share of time to read traffic, or the compute pipe is idle while the read pipe is busy; a cycle estimate showing transfer cycles above compute cycles also qualifies.
common_non_matches: The dominant movement cost is on the store side; that is `write-transfer-pressure`.
The reads are data-dependent and scattered rather than repeated or narrow; that is `irregular-access`.
The loss is a gap between transfer and compute phases rather than total transfer volume; that is `cross-engine-sync-stall`.

symptoms.summary: Store traffic dominates the measured path: fragmented, masked, strided, or multi-destination writes.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Profile attributes a large share of time to store instructions or write bandwidth, or IR/source shows stores issued in small or strided fragments.
common_non_matches: The dominant movement cost is on the load side; that is `read-transfer-pressure`.

symptoms.summary: The same data or the same producer result is loaded, rebuilt, or recomputed multiple times instead of being reused.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Code or IR shows the same read-only input, overlapping window, shared operand, or producer result fetched or recomputed per iteration, per program, or per call; profile shows the repeated traffic or repeated compute it causes.
common_non_matches: The data is reloaded because an on-chip buffer cannot hold the working set; that capacity question is `on-chip-capacity-exceeded`.

symptoms.summary: Time is spent converting data between layouts or materializing intermediates: transposes, permutes, contiguous/copy passes, or full-size intermediates at producer-consumer boundaries.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Code or IR shows transpose/permute/clone/contiguous calls, layout-conversion copies, or a materialized intermediate that exists only to change physical layout or cross a kernel boundary.
common_non_matches: The copy keeps the layout and only stages data between memory levels; that belongs to a transfer-pressure symptom.

symptoms.summary: Hot-path addresses are data-dependent or scattered, so transfers cannot use wide contiguous access.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Runtime index tensors form GM addresses on the hot path, or profile/IR shows gather-like small transfers instead of block copies.
common_non_matches: The addresses are affine and regular but still lowered as gathers or scalar access; that lowering gap is `compiler-lowering-gap`.

symptoms.summary: The kernel executes work whose results are unused: padded lanes or iterations, masked-off regions, whole-invalid programs, repeated algebra, or hidden intermediate tiles.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Loop bounds, masks, or grid shape show iterations, lanes, or programs that cannot affect the output; or the algebra provably repeats work; or profile time sits in instructions whose outputs are discarded.
common_non_matches: The programs are all useful but too small or too few to fill the device; that is `occupancy-underfill`.

symptoms.summary: The compute engines are underutilized: too little math per loaded byte, serialized vector work, or a reduction that never reaches the cube.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Profile shows low compute-pipe utilization relative to other pipes; or a cycle estimate shows transfer cycles exceeding compute cycles; or the hot reduction is scalar/manual instead of a `tl.dot`.
common_non_matches: Per-byte work is fixed and no reuse scales with tile; the kernel is then memory-bound by nature and `read-transfer-pressure` applies.
The engines idle because of cross-engine waiting, not because there is too little math; that is `cross-engine-sync-stall`.

symptoms.summary: The device is not filled: too few or too small programs, uneven program batches, or a long reduction walked serially inside every program.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Program count is near or below the core count, per-program work is a few elements or one row, the final program batch is partially filled, or the grid lacks a reduction-axis factor while the reduction is long.
common_non_matches: Programs are numerous but many are whole-invalid; that is `wasted-or-inactive-work`.
The host launches many small kernels instead of one filled launch; that is `host-launch-overhead`.

symptoms.summary: Compute and transfer phases, or cube and vector cores, wait on each other instead of overlapping.
symptoms.evidence_hint: The timeline shows avoidable gaps between data movement and the compute that consumes it, or flag/wait dependencies serialize phases that have no data dependence.
common_non_matches: The delay comes from a layout conversion between engines, not from synchronization; that is `layout-conversion-overhead`.

symptoms.summary: Scalar or control work (address arithmetic, division/modulo index decode, explicit comparisons) dominates the hot loop instead of vectorized data work.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Profile or IR shows scalar integer instructions, division/modulo, or explicit compare-select chains consuming a large share of the hot loop.
common_non_matches: The repeated work is a loop-invariant recomputation rather than scalar instruction overhead; that is `redundant-data-reload`.

symptoms.summary: The per-program working set (operands, intermediates, accumulators) exceeds the practical UB or on-chip budget.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Tiling or allocation diagnostics show overflow, spills, or compile failures that scale with tile constants or with a single long-lived temporary.

symptoms.summary: Facts the source proves (alignment, contiguity, regular tile shapes) are not used by the compiler lowering, producing gathers, scalar addressing, or extra masks.
symptoms.evidence_hint: IR shows gather or scalar-address lowering for accesses the source can prove affine and aligned, or a regular rectangular tile expressed through scalar pointer arithmetic.
common_non_matches: The access really is data-dependent; that is `irregular-access`.

symptoms.summary: A special-function, normalization, or conversion chain (exp, div, log, rsqrt) sits on the measured critical path.
symptoms.evidence_hint: Profile or IR attributes a large share of time to special-function instructions or to a normalize/convert chain around them.

symptoms.summary: The host repeatedly launches small independent kernels for one logical operation.
symptoms.evidence_hint: The timeline shows many small kernel launches with gaps, each computing a slice of one logical operation.
common_non_matches: One launch whose grid does not fill the device; that is `occupancy-underfill`.
